overview: Bangladesh is a country in South Asia, almost surrounded by India. Its capital and largest city is Dhaka. Bangladesh was the eastern part of Pakistan until it won independence in 1971. It is one of the most densely populated countries in the world and one of the biggest exporters of clothing. Bengali, also called Bangla, is the official language.

geography.text: Most of Bangladesh lies on the delta of three great rivers, the Ganges, the Brahmaputra and the Meghna, and is very low and flat, so floods are common. The summer monsoon brings heavy rain. In the south-west, the Sundarbans, the largest mangrove forest in the world, which Bangladesh shares with India, is home to Bengal tigers, and the country has a long coast on the Bay of Bengal.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Hot and humid, with a heavy monsoon from June to October that often causes floods.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Bengal tigers, spotted deer and river dolphins live in the Sundarbans.

history.text: Bengal was home to powerful kingdoms and later part of the Mughal Empire and British India. When British India was divided in 1947, East Bengal became East Pakistan. Anger at rule from West Pakistan led to the Liberation War of 1971, in which Bangladesh won independence. It has since become one of the world's largest clothing exporters.

events.title: Battle of Plassey
events.text: Britain's East India Company takes control of Bengal.

events.title: Partition
events.text: East Bengal becomes part of Pakistan.

events.title: Language Movement
events.text: Students die protesting for Bengali to be an official language; the date is now International Mother Language Day.

events.title: Nobel Peace Prize
events.text: Muhammad Yunus and the Grameen Bank win the prize for pioneering microcredit.

government.text: Bangladesh is a parliamentary republic in which the Prime Minister leads the government and the President is head of state. In 2024 student-led protests forced Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to resign and flee, and an interim government led by Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus took over, promising reforms and new elections.

economy.text: Bangladesh is the world's second-largest exporter of clothing, after China; garments make up most of its exports. Money sent home by Bangladeshis abroad, farming and a growing IT sector are also important. Its economy has grown quickly for decades.

culture.text: Bangladesh is one of the most densely populated countries on Earth. Bengali, its language, was so important to its identity that its defence led to independence. The poet Rabindranath Tagore, who wrote its national anthem, won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913. The Sundarbans mangrove forest is home to Bengal tigers.

items.title: Sundarbans
items.text: The world's largest mangrove forest, shared with India.

items.title: Language Martyrs' Day
items.text: 21 February, now International Mother Language Day.

items.title: Rickshaw art
items.text: Brightly painted cycle rickshaws, listed by UNESCO.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Rice and fish, especially hilsa, the national fish, cooked in mustard sauce.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: Baul singers, wandering mystic musicians, are listed by UNESCO.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: Pohela Boishakh, Bengali New Year in April, brings colourful processions.

sport.text: Cricket is the most popular sport in Bangladesh, and the national team plays Test cricket. Shakib Al Hasan has been rated the world's best all-rounder. Kabaddi, a tag-and-wrestle team game, is the national sport.

items.title: Shakib Al Hasan
items.text: One of the leading all-rounders in cricket.

didYouKnow: The Sundarbans, shared with India, is the largest mangrove forest in the world.
21 February, Bangladesh's Language Martyrs' Day, is now International Mother Language Day.

keyPeople.name: Rabindranath Tagore
keyPeople.text: Wrote Bangladesh's national anthem; won the Nobel Prize in 1913.

keyPeople.name: Muhammad Yunus
keyPeople.text: Won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2006 for microcredit.
